explanation: The Almighty Creator who is the source of all miracles, teaching, and salvation described in the chapter.
The teacher from Nazareth who preaches God's kingdom, heals the sick, and calms storms with his word.
The many parables Jesus tells about how people hear God's word and let it grow in their hearts.
The person who sows the seed (God's word) along the path, among rocks, thorns, and good soil to show different responses.
A symbol of God's message or the gospel being spread to people with varying responses.
The place where the seed falls without taking root, represented by those who hear but do not understand and have the word taken away from them.
Hard places where the seed sprouts quickly but withers because it lacks deep roots, symbolizing faith that lasts only in good times.
Plant growth that chokes the seed by taking its nutrients, representing worries and the riches of the world.
The use refers to people with a pure heart who hear the word, keep it, and bear fruit through patience.
The violent calming of the wind on the sea, showing Jesus' power over nature and creating fear among the disciples.
The evil spirits living in a man outside society, but driven out by Jesus into the pigs.
A herd of animals that rush down into the sea after the possessed men are healed and the demons are allowed to enter them.
The sick woman with bleeding for twelve years who is made well when she touches Jesus' cloak, illustrating the power of faith.
A synagogue leader whose daughter is dying, whom Jesus raises from the dead after hearing about the event.
Jesus' journey through cities and villages to preach the kingdom of God to many people along the way.
